page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz with x86_64 architecture, providing 32 physical cores and 64 virtual CPUs with dedicated CPU allocation. The system is configured with 2048.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, delivering a memory density of 32.0 GB per vCPU core. Included local storage comprises 1900 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage. Network performance provides a 50 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Supported CPU instruction set features include AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and Total Memory Encryption.

In benchmark evaluations, the x2iedn.16xlarge displays strong multi-core computational performance, achieving top-tier benchmark results in stress-ng multi-core testing, PassMark CPU evaluation, software compilation using Clang, and PassMark encryption tests. Database operations performance and small-to-medium model LLM text generation speeds also rank in the top performance tier. Conversely, single-core processing scores, memory bandwidth measurements, and static web serving throughput fall into average benchmark tiers, indicating that workload performance relies on multi-core scaling rather than individual core throughput.

From a resource efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU density allows memory-heavy applications to run on a consolidated footprint without requiring multi-node distribution. The combination of 2048.0 GB RAM and high-speed local NVMe SSD storage targets workloads requiring significant memory capacity alongside fast local scratch space. Appropriate workload fits include large in-memory databases, complex database operations, real-time data processing, and enterprise software compilation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by a 32-core Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs, 2048.0 GB of DDR4 RAM at 3 GHz, 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core CPU capabilities, with top-tier results in multi-core stress tests, PassMark CPU and encryption benchmarks, Clang software compilation, and database operations. Single-core speeds and memory bandwidth benchmarks remain within average ranges, highlighting a design that emphasizes multi-threaded parallel execution over single-thread velocity. The substantial memory allocation offers qualitative cost efficiency by consolidating large memory requirements onto a single node. The server is well-suited for enterprise in-memory databases, heavy database processing, and data-intensive applications.
